faqs.q: What is the Guillemin female thread adapter used for?
faqs.a: The Guillemin female thread adapter has a Guillemin head without a lock ring on one end and a female pipe thread on the other, so a Guillemin hose line can be tied to a male threaded nipple, valve or pump port.

faqs.q: Which sizes is the Guillemin female thread adapter available in?
faqs.a: The Guillemin female thread adapter is listed in sizes from 3/4" to 4" (the maker's published Guillemin size range). This listing has no size table, so quote the size you need and the hose or thread it connects to, and we confirm the match and the manufacturer part number before supply.

faqs.q: How should I select the Guillemin female thread adapter for my application?
faqs.a: Choose the size, 3/4" to 4", then the thread type and size of the male fitting it must take, and the body material. This adapter has no lock ring; if you want one on the Guillemin head, see the coupling with female thread.

faqs.q: What working pressure applies to the Guillemin female thread adapter?
faqs.a: The maker publishes no working pressure for the Guillemin female thread adapter. The pressure the joint can carry depends on the size, the gasket and the hose tail, so give us your working pressure and medium through [our contact page](/contact) and we check it with the maker before you order.

faqs.q: Which materials is the Guillemin female thread adapter offered in?
faqs.a: The Guillemin female thread adapter is made in aluminium or stainless steel. Choose aluminium for light handling on water, fire and general transfer and stainless steel where the fluid or the environment is corrosive. Confirm the body material in the enquiry because the part number depends on it.

faqs.q: Which standards and documents apply to the Guillemin female thread adapter?
faqs.a: The Guillemin system is standardised in France as NF E 29-572, but the maker does not state which standard the Guillemin female thread adapter is made to, and no certificates are held on this listing. If you need a conformity statement or material report, say so in the enquiry and we ask the maker what it can issue. Our [guide to Guillemin couplings](/blog/guillemin-couplings-explained) explains the system.

faqs.q: What does the Guillemin female thread adapter connect to?
faqs.a: The Guillemin head joins any Guillemin head of the same size, and the female thread takes a male pipe nipple. See [the Guillemin male thread adapter](/p/guillemin-adapter-male-thread) for the other gender and [the Guillemin short shank coupling](/p/guillemin-coupling-short-shank) for the hose side.

faqs.q: How should the Guillemin female thread adapter be installed and maintained?
faqs.a: Check the gasket in the Guillemin female thread adapter at each make-up, because it is the wear part of the joint. Guillemin heads are quarter-turn and symmetrical, and a lock ring stops the joint turning apart in service where one is fitted. Clamp any hose tail for the pressure the hose will see. Guillemin does not interchange with Storz, cam and groove or Barcelona couplings.

faqs.q: Where is the Guillemin female thread adapter used?
faqs.a: Guillemin couplings are widely used in France on fire, water and industrial transfer hose. The Guillemin female thread adapter suits the same duties, including water supply, fire-fighting hose lines and general industrial fluid transfer where a symmetrical quarter-turn joint is wanted.

faqs.q: How does the Guillemin female thread adapter differ from the Guillemin coupling with female thread?
faqs.a: The adapter has a Guillemin head without a lock ring, while [the Guillemin coupling with female thread](/p/guillemin-coupling-female-thread) has a Guillemin head listed as the coupling version of the same female-thread connection, with the maker's MKF note. Both end in a female thread; choose by whether you want the plain head or the coupling pattern.

The pressure the joint can carry depends on the size, the gasket and the hose tail, so give us your working pressure and medium through [our contact page](/contact) and we check it with the maker before you order.

faqs.q: What is the Guillemin coupling with short shank made from?
faqs.a: The Guillemin coupling with short shank is made in aluminium or stainless steel. Choose aluminium for light handling on water, fire and general transfer and stainless steel where the fluid or the environment is corrosive. Confirm the body material in the enquiry because the part number depends on it.

faqs.q: Which standards apply to the Guillemin coupling with short shank?
faqs.a: The Guillemin system is standardised in France as NF E 29-572, but the maker does not state which standard the Guillemin coupling with short shank is made to, and no certificates are held on this listing. If you need a conformity statement or material report, say so in the enquiry and we ask the maker what it can issue. Our [guide to Guillemin couplings](/blog/guillemin-couplings-explained) explains the system.

faqs.q: What does the Guillemin coupling with short shank connect to?
faqs.a: The Guillemin head joins any Guillemin head of the same size, and the shank goes into a hose secured with a clamp. See [the Guillemin coupling with long hose shank](/p/guillemin-coupling-long-hose-shank) for the longer version.

faqs.q: How should the Guillemin coupling with short shank be installed and maintained?
faqs.a: Check the gasket in the Guillemin coupling with short shank at each make-up, because it is the wear part of the joint. Guillemin heads are quarter-turn and symmetrical, and a lock ring stops the joint turning apart in service where one is fitted. Clamp any hose tail for the pressure the hose will see. Guillemin does not interchange with Storz, cam and groove or Barcelona couplings.

faqs.q: Which industries and jobs use the Guillemin coupling with short shank?
faqs.a: Guillemin couplings are widely used in France on fire, water and industrial transfer hose. The Guillemin coupling with short shank suits the same duties, including water supply, fire-fighting hose lines and general industrial fluid transfer where a symmetrical quarter-turn joint is wanted.

faqs.q: How does the Guillemin coupling with short shank differ from the Guillemin coupling with long hose shank?
faqs.a: The short shank saves length and suits flexible hose, while [the Guillemin coupling with long hose shank](/p/guillemin-coupling-long-hose-shank) has a longer shank for more hose support. Both have a Guillemin head with a lock ring in 3/4" to 4".
